evidence.diagnosticTask: Examine a square, rectangle, scalene triangle and an irregular quadrilateral. Test each shape for symmetry and identify every line of symmetry that exists.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Identify and justify lines of symmetry in fresh regular and irregular 2D shapes.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, test fresh 2D shapes and identify their lines of symmetry.
evidence.transferTask: Examine several simple geometric patterns used in a design. Determine which are symmetrical and show the line or lines of symmetry.

specs.title: Describe Position and Motion Using Cardinal Points
specs.description: Tell the position and motion of objects in space using the cardinal points.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Using a simple map with north marked, identify north, south, east and west. Describe the position of one object relative to another and describe a movement from one location to another using cardinal points.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Describe positions and movements on fresh maps or diagrams using the correct cardinal points.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, identify cardinal points and describe relative position and movement on a fresh diagram.
evidence.transferTask: On a school map, the library is east of the classroom and the field is north of the library. Describe the positions and directions needed to move between these places.

specs.title: Estimate Perimeter
specs.description: Estimate perimeter using referents for centimetres or metres.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Estimate the perimeter of a classroom tabletop using suitable centimetre or metre referents. Estimate each side length and then estimate the total boundary length.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Estimate the perimeters of fresh objects and shapes using appropriate centimetre or metre referents.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, select a suitable length referent and estimate the perimeter of a fresh object.
evidence.transferTask: Estimate how many metres of edging would be needed to go around a small rectangular garden before measuring it.

specs.title: Measure Perimeter
specs.description: Measure and record perimeter of regular and irregular shapes in centimetres and metres.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Measure all sides of a regular shape and an irregular shape, add the boundary lengths and record each perimeter with the correct unit.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Measure and record the perimeters of fresh regular and irregular shapes in centimetres or metres.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, measure every boundary side of a fresh shape and calculate its perimeter.
evidence.transferTask: Measure the boundary of a classroom notice board and determine its perimeter, recording the answer with the correct unit.

specs.title: Use Perimeter Formulae
specs.description: Develop and apply a formula for determining the perimeter of a square and rectangle.

evidence.diagnosticTask: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide, and a square has side length 6 cm. Derive the perimeter rule for each shape and use it to calculate both perimeters.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Derive and apply perimeter formulae to fresh squares and rectangles.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, state and apply the perimeter rules for a fresh square and rectangle.
evidence.transferTask: A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 7 m wide. Use the perimeter formula to determine the length of fencing required around it.

specs.title: Construct Rectangles with a Given Perimeter
specs.description: Construct different rectangles for a given perimeter and recognise that many shapes can have the same perimeter.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Construct at least three different rectangles with a perimeter of 20 cm. Find valid side-length pairs and compare the resulting rectangles.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Construct different rectangles for fresh given perimeters and explain why different shapes can have the same perimeter.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, find multiple rectangles having the same specified perimeter.
evidence.transferTask: A farmer has 24 m of fencing for a rectangular plot. Find different possible length and width pairs and compare the rectangles.

specs.title: Recognise Square Units of Area
specs.description: Recognise that area is measured in square units.

evidence.diagnosticTask: A rectangular region is completely covered by equal square tiles. Count the square units covering the region and explain why its area is measured in square units rather than units of length.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Determine the areas of fresh regions by counting square units and distinguish area units from length units.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, count the square units covering a fresh region and state its area using the correct unit.
evidence.transferTask: A tabletop diagram is covered exactly by 24 equal square units. State its area and explain what the 24 square units measure.

specs.title: Select Area Referents
specs.description: Select and justify referents for square centimetres or square metres.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Choose an appropriate area referent for a small book cover and for a classroom floor. Explain when a square centimetre or square metre is the better unit.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Select and justify suitable square centimetre or square metre referents for fresh surfaces.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, choose suitable area referents for a small and a large surface and justify each choice.
evidence.transferTask: Choose the appropriate square unit for estimating the area of a phone screen and the area of a classroom floor, and explain why.

specs.title: Estimate Area
specs.description: Estimate area using referents for square centimetres or square metres.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Estimate the area of a book cover using square centimetres and the area of a classroom floor using square metres. Explain the referent and estimated number of square units used.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Estimate the areas of fresh surfaces using suitable square centimetre or square metre referents.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, choose an area referent and estimate the number of square units covering a fresh surface.
evidence.transferTask: Estimate the area of a classroom notice board using an appropriate square-unit referent and state the estimated area.

specs.title: Use Area Formulae
specs.description: Develop and apply a formula for determining the area of a rectangle and square.

evidence.diagnosticTask: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide, and a square has side length 5 cm. Derive the area rule for each shape and calculate both areas.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Derive and apply the area formulae to fresh rectangles and squares.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, state and apply the area rules for a fresh rectangle and square.
evidence.transferTask: A rectangular garden is 9 m long and 6 m wide. Use the appropriate area formula to determine its area.

specs.title: Construct Rectangles with a Given Area
specs.description: Construct different rectangles for a given area and recognise that different rectangles may have the same area.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Construct at least three different rectangles with an area of 24 square units. Find valid factor pairs and compare the resulting rectangles.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Construct different rectangles for a fresh given area and explain why different dimensions can produce the same area.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, find multiple rectangles having the same specified area.
evidence.transferTask: A rectangular garden must have an area of 36 square metres. Find different possible length and width pairs and compare the shapes.

specs.title: Read Analogue, Digital and 24-Hour Time
specs.description: Tell time in hours and minutes on analogue and digital watches, including 24-hour clocks.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Read times shown on analogue and digital clocks, interpret a 24-hour time, and convert between 12-hour and 24-hour formats.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Read and convert fresh analogue, digital and 24-hour time examples.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, read fresh clock displays and convert between time formats.
evidence.transferTask: A school programme begins at 14:30. State the time in 12-hour format and show how it would appear on an analogue clock.

specs.title: Measure Event Duration
specs.description: Use a clock to measure the time taken to complete simple events in minutes and seconds.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Record the start and end times of a short activity, calculate the elapsed time and state the duration using minutes or seconds.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Measure and calculate the duration of fresh events from their start and end times.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, determine the elapsed time for a fresh event and state the correct unit.
evidence.transferTask: A pupil starts an exercise at 10:15 and finishes at 10:42. Calculate the duration and state it with the correct unit.

specs.title: Record Calendar Dates
specs.description: State dates of events and record calendar dates in a variety of formats.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Identify a date on a calendar, associate it with an event and write the same date in more than one accepted format.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Identify and record fresh calendar dates in different formats and associate each date with the correct event.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, identify a fresh calendar date and write it correctly in multiple formats.
evidence.transferTask: A school event is scheduled for 19 September 2026. Locate the date on a calendar and record it in different accepted formats.

specs.title: Read and Interpret One-to-One Graphs
specs.description: Use one-to-one correspondence to read and interpret graphs.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Read a one-to-one graph in which each symbol represents one item. Identify the categories, determine their values and explain what the graph shows.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Read and interpret a fresh one-to-one graph, correctly linking each symbol to one unit.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, read category values from a fresh one-to-one graph and interpret the information.
evidence.transferTask: A class pictograph shows favourite fruits with one symbol representing one pupil. Determine the number of pupils in each category and explain which fruit is most and least popular.

specs.title: Construct Many-to-One Graphs
specs.description: Use many-to-one correspondence to display or construct graphs.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Given category data and a key where one symbol represents several items, convert the data into scaled symbols and construct a correctly labelled many-to-one graph.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Construct a fresh many-to-one graph from data using the supplied key and correct labels.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, interpret a graph key and construct a many-to-one graph from fresh data.
evidence.transferTask: A class survey records 20, 15 and 10 pupils in three categories. Using a key where one symbol represents 5 pupils, construct and label a many-to-one graph.

specs.title: Compare Different Graph Displays
specs.description: Compare graphs showing the same data and explain how they are the same and different.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Compare two graphs that display the same data using different scales or structures. Identify the matching data and explain how the displays are the same and different.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Compare fresh graph displays of the same data, including their scales, structures and presentation differences.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, compare two fresh graphs showing the same data and explain their similarities and differences.
evidence.transferTask: Two newspapers display the same survey results using different graph scales. Compare the graphs and explain why they represent the same data despite looking different.

specs.title: Identify Many-to-One Graphs in Media
specs.description: Find examples of graphs using many-to-one correspondence in print and electronic media and describe the correspondence used.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Examine examples from print or electronic media, identify a graph using many-to-one correspondence, locate its key or scale and explain what one symbol or unit represents.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Identify fresh many-to-one graphs from real-world media and describe the correspondence shown by each key or scale.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, identify a many-to-one graph and explain its key or scale.
evidence.transferTask: Find or examine a graph from a newspaper, website or school notice and determine whether it uses many-to-one correspondence. Explain the correspondence value.

specs.title: Construct Pictographs and Bar Graphs
specs.description: Identify common graph features and construct bar graphs or pictographs with title, labelled axes, key or legend.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Given a set of category data, select an appropriate scale and construct a bar graph or pictograph with a title, correctly labelled axes and a key or legend.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Construct a fresh bar graph or pictograph from supplied data with all required graph features.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, construct and correctly label a graph from fresh category data.
evidence.transferTask: Use class survey data to construct a clear bar graph or pictograph that another pupil can interpret without additional explanation.

specs.title: Solve Problems Using Many-to-One Graphs
specs.description: Use many-to-one correspondence to solve simple problems requiring interpretation of many-to-one bar graphs.

evidence.diagnosticTask: Read a many-to-one bar graph, apply its scale to calculate category quantities, compare categories and solve a question based on the graph.
evidence.reassessmentTask: Solve fresh problems requiring interpretation and comparison of quantities in many-to-one graphs.
evidence.retentionTask: Without reviewing the lesson, apply the scale of a fresh many-to-one graph and solve a graph-based problem.
evidence.transferTask: A school graph shows books read by four classes, with each graph unit representing 5 books. Calculate the quantities, compare the classes and answer a problem using the graph.
